newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close higher on cash support.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close higher on cash support.

text.p: CME lumber futures traded uneven much of the day in light trade but finished mostly higher on support from firmer cash, traders said.

Cash spruce prices continued to drift higher, offsetting concern over interest rates and rolling of long positions from November into January. Spruce will likely be quoted in the $375 to $380 per tbf area Friday, up from Wednesday's midweek quote of $372, traders said.
Lower bond markets kept a lid on lumber futures as higher interest rates would likely reduce consumer demand for housing, they added.
Lumber closed $4.00 per tbf higher to $0.90 lower with November up $1.60 at $365.70 and January up most at $374.50 per tbf.
